newsitem.title: POLAND: Poland offers PLN 800 mln of fixed bonds on Feb 5.
newsitem.headline: Poland offers PLN 800 mln of fixed bonds on Feb 5.

text.p: Poland will offer 800 million zlotys from a new series of fixed two-year 15 percent bonds and five-year 12 percent bonds at a tender on February 5, 1997, the finance ministry said.
It said in a statement the value date for the shorter, two-year paper, due June 12, 1999, is February 12, 1997 and the same value date is for the longer, five-year bond, due June 12, 2002.
The coupon of the shorter paper, at 16 percent for previous issues, is set at 15 percent for this issue.

The Finance Ministry's Lidia Moronczyk told Reuters that was because the ministry wants to assimilate in June this year this issue of the two-year bonds into a 1994 issue of five year bonds which has the same maturity on June 12, 1999, and had a coupon of 15 percent.
The bonds come from a new three billion zloty issue of two- and five-year fixed bonds which will be offered at four consecutive tenders in from February to May.

The ministry moved the deadline for this auction to 1100 local time (1000 GMT) from the regular 1200 to announce the results earlier than usual and so that investors could start payment procedures on the day of the tender.
